# lernapps.net tooling

> Build, check and list learning apps for lernapps.net with an AI assistant. The package @lernapps/tooling is on npm.

## Before you start: check the entry criteria

1. **A shell:** you can run commands, with Node 22.18 or newer, git, and `npm` reaching npmjs.com. If not (a chat in
   the browser, such as chatgpt.com, usually cannot): **stop here and do nothing else.** Tell the creator in two
   sentences that this does not work in this environment and that they should start again in one that does, such as
   the desktop application of their AI assistant, with the same request. Do not build the app by hand from this page.
2. **`npx` may run:** your harness lets you run `npx --yes @lernapps/tooling …` (it runs a package from npm). If its
   permissions block it (an auto mode that refuses code from the internet), tell the creator in two sentences how to
   allow it, e.g. in Claude Code a permission rule `Bash(npx --yes @lernapps/tooling:*)`, and wait. Never work around
   the block. Until it is allowed, start with the fallback below; building the app (Code) needs `npx`.
3. **An empty folder:** the app is the folder you start in. Work in it, never in a subfolder.

## Build an app

1. In the empty folder run `npx --yes @lernapps/tooling init <short name>`. It writes the plan template, complete and
   unchanged, as `.vibe/plans/01-<short name>.md`, `AGENTS.md` (every process rule, also below on this page),
   `CLAUDE.md` and the skills of the phases.
2. Read the plan in full. Follow it task by task: it gives the order, names the skills of each phase and holds the
   creator's checkpoints. The process rules of `AGENTS.md` hold in every phase.

Read guidance from the file, in full. Nothing is downloaded: a fetch tool that summarises loses tasks and rules, and
`init` copies the files as they are.

### Fallback: without `npx`, for Explore and Plan

When `npx` may not run yet, the same files come from the repository https://github.com/lernapps/tooling:

1. `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/lernapps/tooling` into a temporary folder, not into the app's folder.
2. Copy into the app's folder, unchanged: `guidance/plan-template.md` as `.vibe/plans/01-<short name>.md`,
   `guidance/AGENTS.md` as `AGENTS.md`; write `CLAUDE.md` with the one line `@AGENTS.md`; copy the folders
   `skills/process/*`, `skills/content/*` and `skills/tooling/*` into `.agents/skills/` (each skill a folder with its
   `SKILL.md`).
3. Follow the plan through Explore and Plan. Before Code, `npx` must run: in the same folder, `npx --yes
   @lernapps/tooling init <short name>` (the same short name) installs the packages and writes the files again; it
   keeps the plan you filled in. Without the packages there is no app.

## Change a published app

- In the app's repo, `AGENTS.md` leads to the current plan and the increment template.

## Reference

Look things up here when you need them. Not needed for building.

- Rules by id: https://lernapps.net/tooling/rules/ (check messages link `#<id>`).
- Platform rules for an app built without this tooling (by hand, another framework, an app builder):
  node_modules/@lernapps/tooling/skills/tooling/lernapps-cli/references/platform-rules.md (after `npx --yes @lernapps/tooling init`)
- Check a built or published app: `npx --yes @lernapps/tooling check <dir|url>`. Every
  command lists its options with `--help`.
- Schemas: validation report https://lernapps.net/tooling/schemas/validation-report.v1.schema.json, review verdict
  https://lernapps.net/tooling/schemas/verdict.v1.schema.json, catalog entry
  https://lernapps.net/apps/schemas/entry.v1.schema.json. The schemas of a quiz and of an explainer are in the app:
  node_modules/@lernapps/app-templates/runtime/quiz/quiz.v1.schema.json and .../explainer/explainer.v1.schema.json.
- GitHub, explained for creators: https://lernapps.net/tooling/github/
- Keeping an app up to date, the two GitHub Apps and the settings: https://lernapps.net/tooling/github/updates/
- Which assistant to build with, and three apps a budget model built: https://lernapps.net/tooling/assistants/
- How we test the guidance, with eval results: https://lernapps.net/tooling/prompt-engineering/
- Architecture: https://lernapps.net/tooling/architecture/

## Other llms.txt of lernapps.net

- lernapps.net, where to find what: https://lernapps.net/llms.txt
- Docs: https://lernapps.net/docs/llms.txt
- Catalog: https://lernapps.net/apps/llms.txt; listing an app: https://lernapps.net/apps/enter/llms.txt

The process rules follow below: `AGENTS.md`, the file `init` writes into every app, as it is in this version.

## AGENTS.md

Learning app for lernapps.net: static, runs in the browser, collects nothing, accessible. Built with its creator.

### Start here

1. Current plan: `.vibe/plans/<NN>-<short name>.md` with the highest NN.
2. No plan, or its Commit is completed: start a new plan. Copy a template complete and unchanged from
   `@lernapps/tooling/guidance/` (in `node_modules/`):
   - `plan-template.md`: the first version;
   - `increment-template.md`: every later change.
3. Read the plan before each step. Do its tasks in order. Each phase names its skills. The plan gives the order; the
   process rules below hold in every phase.

### Folder

- The app is the folder where `lernapps init` ran: this file, `CLAUDE.md` and `.vibe/` are in it. `lernapps create`
  and every command run there, never in a subfolder or a copy.

### Always

- Read guidance and skills from the file, in full. Never use a fetch tool that summarises.
- Push only the branch the current plan names. A push to `main` publishes.
- Tick a box only after you did what it says, and only as far as it says. A box you did in part stays open, with a line
  saying what is missing.
- Never `--no-verify`. Never edit `prePushFailures` or `failedChecks`.
- Never edit a `lernapps-*` skill: `lernapps update` replaces them. The app's own skills (`app-content`, `app-*`)
  take precedence; app rules go there.
- Nothing about a real learner in any file or commit message (`no-learner-data-in-texts`).

### Process rules

Each rule in full, with examples: `@lernapps/tooling/guidance/workflow-rules.md` (in `node_modules/`) and
https://lernapps.net/tooling/rules/.

<!-- process rules: written by scripts/agents-md.ts from guidance/workflow-rules.md -->

| Rule | What | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `plan-file` | Keep the plan file | Each plan in `.vibe/plans/`, with every section and front matter key of its template. Never change the plan of an earlier piece of work. Set `phase` when you enter a phase. Tick each task box when it is done. Never edit `prePushFailures` or `failedChecks`: the hook and the check write them. |
| `explore-before-code` | No code before the plan is confirmed | No code and no `lernapps create` until the creator has confirmed the plan with a yes. |
| `stop-at-checkpoints` | Stop at the creator's checkpoints | Checkpoints: research, confirm the plan and the content method, the pattern page (`early-preview`), publish. Stop at each and wait for the answer. Checkpoint list: open the listing pull request first (it publishes nothing), then show it and its result and wait. A message sent before the checkpoint's question is no yes. |
| `few-turns-after-plan` | Work on your own after the plan | After the confirmation, ask only what you cannot decide. Else choose, mark "(guess)" under "Key decisions" and list it in the retrospective. |
| `early-preview` | A pattern page first, with the creator's look | In Code, build one complete page or screen first: the pattern for the others. An explainer: entry, figure or model, how learners use it, example, exercise. Before you show it, check it: against the rules of skill `lernapps-<archetype>-design` (an explainer: the five questions of `explainer-representation-explained` for each figure and model), and let a sub-agent use it in the browser as a learner of the app's grade (`@lernapps/tooling/guidance/subagent-brief.md`, "Learner check"). The app must run for it: start `npm run dev` as a background task of your harness (a process started with `nohup … &` in a shell that ends dies with it), and check that its address answers before the sub-agent starts. Run the sub-agent in the foreground and wait for its report in the same turn; no turn ends while it runs. No sub-agent tool: do the learner check yourself, in the browser, with the same brief. Fix what they find. Look at the screenshots yourself, each image (`npx --no -- lernapps screenshots --desktop`, desktop and 360 px): what you have not seen you cannot show. Your tools cannot show an image (a read gives only bytes): check the page in the browser instead (its text, the boxes of its elements at both widths) and say so to the creator. Then send the creator one message that begins "**Code · Checkpoint** Zwischenstand": the screenshots (their paths, or the images where the chat shows them), on the creator's machine also the address of `npm run dev`, started in the background; what learners do on the page in one or two sentences; one question: may the other pages follow this pattern? A checkpoint: wait for the answer. Every message after it is the creator's answer. A change → change the pattern first, then build the other pages after it. |
| `feedback-applied-everywhere` | A remark on one page is checked on all | The creator remarks on one page, figure or component: say whether it is about that place or a pattern ("Gilt das für alle Seiten?" only when you cannot tell). A pattern → find every place that follows it (the same component, block type or wording) and change them all in the same task. A fix in a shared component: look at every page that uses it again. |
| `retrospective-filled` | Fill the retrospective | At the end of Commit, fill every part with facts: phases reached, creator turns after the plan, where you guessed. No names. Failed checks need no entry: the check counts them in `failedChecks`. |
| `app-content-guide` | Keep the app's content guide | Keep `.agents/skills/app-content/SKILL.md` with its fixed headings, in this order, each filled: Curriculum, Competencies, Content structure, Terminology, Exercise patterns, Figures, Sources, Adding a chapter or round, Rules learned from mistakes ("None yet." until the first rule). After the plan is confirmed and before content: replace every placeholder ("FILL IN") with concrete instructions for writing new content: files, ids, data files, an example of this app. Not how the app works, no general advice. A content decision changes (pattern, figure type, source rule) → change the guide in the same commit. `lernapps check` checks the file and its headings always, and that no placeholder is left once the plan is in Commit. App older than the guide: `lernapps update` adds the skeleton (skill `lernapps-cli`). |
| `app-content-matches` | The content guide says what was built | Every pattern it names is used; no pattern is used that it does not name. Curriculum, competencies, chapters, pages or rounds match the content. Its procedure for a new chapter or round names the current files. An agent without your conversation can add the next chapter or round from it alone. |

<!-- end of the process rules -->

### Language

- Learners, teachers, parents: German, plain language.
- Creator: their language, plain words, no forms.
